At the same time, there was a wish, within myself and also clearly expressed in a number of parliamentary motions, to make changes on a number of points.
Mr De Vries has submitted motions to enable an investment impulse aimed at cheap rental properties and to expand the scheme for South Rotterdam. There was also a wish, which was widely supported, to add the new shrinking regions to the reduction of the landlord levy. There was also a widespread desire to partially exempt small landlords and thus also courtyards from the landlord levy or, if that is not entirely successful, to grant them a lower levy on balance. Although I heard some criticism from Mr Van Vliet, I have indeed included in this proposal a scheme for taking over private property in shrinking regions. I will respond to his amendment later. However, I dispute that I did nothing at all with his two motions.
After this introduction, I will discuss three themes that have been raised by almost everyone, namely the elaboration of the WOZ as a basis for the levy, the questions that have been asked regarding the regional elaboration and a number of other questions. Finally, I will address the amendments that have already been tabled. I understand there are more to come. I will respond to this in writing.
First of all, the questions relating to the WOZ as a basis. Mr Ronnes stated that the increase in the WOZ value, at least in part of the country, means that the levy yields much more than initially estimated. That is not the case. The revenues from the levy are actually in line with the forecast we made, because we also assumed an increasing WOZ value. So there is no extra revenue. If this does occur, it will be, as the technicians call it, an endogenous development and therefore no revenue that can then be used for spending.
Mr Ronnes, Mr Bashir, Mr Van Vliet and I believe also Mr De Vries asked about the effect of the high WOZ value in a number of scarcity areas, which would put a heavier burden on the levy there. The evaluation and also the COELO report that was commissioned by the VNG and Aedes - which had a bit of a lobbying purpose, but that is allowed - shows that it is not the case that corporations that are active in an area with a high WOZ value therefore have difficulty with affordability. This could well be the case because during this period of government we have also changed the housing valuation system in such a way that it includes a WOZ component, so that rents can move with that WOZ value.
From the perspective of affordability, there is therefore no reason to differentiate. That doesn't mean I don't see the need in some parts of the country being greater than others. Mr Koolmees specifically addressed this. That is also the reason that this bill contains an additional reduction on the levy. In any case, it is aimed at affordable rental properties, because too much has been invested in expensive rental properties in recent years. This discount is extra large in areas where the housing market is tight. That is also the elegant way. This encourages investments in the homes that the housing associations really support, and you do not have to alter the WOZ basis. I will discuss this in more detail in my response to the motion that concerns this.

Chair. This debate request has actually been running since 2012. Since then, many reports have emerged about the use of chemicals in the Chemours factory, the former DuPont. Several issues are at stake here. On Sliedrecht24 you can read quite a bit in the regional media.
At issue is PFOA, perfluorooctanoic acid, which I will henceforth call C8 and which is used in the production of Teflon. Local residents have been exposed to this for years. Also at issue are the years of exposure of employees to the substance DMAc in the Lycra factory, the licensing by the province, threatened lawsuits by the drinking water company, a multi-million claim from residents living near the company and the alternative substance GenX, the replacement for PFOA or C8, and its discharge into surface water. All this reporting has led to concerns for local residents, employees and former employees. I understand that completely.
Suppose you have been living with your family for years under the smoke of a factory just across the Merwede in Sliedrecht. A good friend of yours worked in that factory for years. She has just retired and has health problems. You may not have had any problems yet, but some time ago you donated blood because you took part in a random sample from the RIVM. Then you get the report from the RIVM, which states, and you read it: there continues to be scientific discussion about what a safe level of exposure is; it is not easy to determine whether this has led to adverse health effects in the past or now; local residents may have experienced adverse effects. It is crucial for the VVD that all people in Sliedrecht, Papendrecht and Dordrecht receive clarity.
The RIVM has conducted research, but the recent report and the conclusions from the RIVM research do not provide that clarity. This requires additional research. That's frustrating, but it's true. I would like to hear from the State Secretary what the plan is. When will these people get clarity? And what is the status of the SZW Inspectorate's investigation when it comes to former and current employees?
Then the fabric C8. The standard has been exceeded by no less than 32 years. How has the situation been allowed to continue for so long? Of course, the ball is primarily in the company's court, but who should have sounded the alarm? Who should have enforced it? Why didn't that happen?
In recent years, the supervisory authority has become more professional. We have formed inspection services. Is that actually the solution to prevent these kinds of things? C8 has now been banned, but questions arise about the replacement substance GenX. You need new research for that. That investigation will take another year. In light of this, I think it is good that the province of South Holland has decided to adjust the permit, simply as a precaution, to ensure that less GenX is discharged.
The company and the new director try to show commitment, but trust is gone. The company has a major communication problem, but even worse is that the neighborhood has a major problem with toxic substances in their environment. This is an undesirable situation. We cannot allay this concern simply by providing information. So it's going to be a long time and maybe a long battle. The VVD wants to know from the State Secretary what else we can do to reduce the unrest. The VVD wants clarity and transparency of information.
We naturally want to prevent these types of situations. How are we going to ensure that? How is it arranged now? Can such a bizarrely long exceedance of 32 years like this be prevented? It is of the utmost importance to learn lessons. Which ones are they?

Dank u wel, voorzitter. Op 24 november jongstleden schreef ik uw Kamer op initiatief van het kabinet een brief waarin ik nog eens op een rij heb gezet wat de regels in ons land zijn op het gebied van seksuele intimidatie en geweld. Daarin heb ik ook uiteengezet hoe we dat kunnen voorkomen en tegengaan in de samenleving, op de werkplek, in het onderwijs, in de sport, maar ook hoe we slachtoffers van seksuele intimidatie en geweld kunnen helpen, in de justitieketen maar ook gewoon in het leven. Die brief kwam voort uit de eerder die maand flink opgelaaide — ik kan niet zeggen "ontstane" — #MeToo-discussie.
Ik ga niet herhalen wat ik in die brief heb geschreven, maar ik wil vanavond toch kort nog even het misverstand wegnemen dat er sprake zou zijn van onduidelijke normen voor seksuele intimidatie. Over verkrachting en aanranding, heel kort gezegd seksueel geweld, zijn we het, denk ik, wel eens in de samenleving, zeker over verkrachting. Dat is duidelijk geformuleerd in het strafrecht in artikel 242. Aanranding staat in artikel 246. Ik wil voor alle duidelijkheid tot nog maar eens zeggen: aanranding, dat is elke afgedwongen, ontuchtige handeling.
In de afgelopen maanden werd hier en daar in het debat, althans soms in de media, door mensen gesuggereerd dat er geen duidelijke norm voor seksuele intimidatie zou zijn. Dat is niet juist, want die norm is er. In de Algemene Wet Gelijke Behandeling staat in ongeveer deze bewoordingen de volgende definitie van seksuele intimidatie: seksuele intimidatie is elke vorm van ongewenst verbaal, non-verbaal of fysiek seksueel getint gedrag met het doel of gevolg de waardigheid van een ander persoon te schenden. En dat dan, kun je zeggen, in het bijzonder door het creëren van een intimiderende, vijandige, onterende of vernederende omgeving. Het punt dat hier in het midden staat, is het schenden van de waardigheid van een ander door bepaald seksueel getint gedrag. Dat is seksuele intimidatie. Dat geeft, denk ik, voldoende houvast om te weten hoever je kunt gaan of — nog beter - welke grenzen je echt niet moet overschrijden.
Ik wil daarbij zeggen, hoewel ik op zichzelf wel interesse heb voor de gedachte die mevrouw Van Toorenburg heeft geuit, dat er ook wel degelijk in het strafrecht een aantal normen zijn op dat gebied. Ik noem schennis van de eerbaarheid in artikel 239 Strafrecht — dat is een licht zedenmisdrijf — of seksueel intimiderend gedrag in de vorm van dwang, bedreiging of belediging. Dat staat ook allemaal in Strafrecht geregeld. Ik ga u niet lastigvallen met het opnoemen van de nummers.
Voorzitter. Ik zie mezelf nou niet echt als een moraalridder. De monitor Seksuele gezondheid bijvoorbeeld geeft gewoon duidelijk aan dat er nog voldoende te verbeteren valt.

Dank voor de zakdoek. Het is niet de emotie, maar het is het weer.

Thank you, Chairman. On November 24, I wrote a letter to your House at the initiative of the cabinet in which I once again listed the rules in our country in the field of sexual harassment and violence. In it I also explained how we can prevent and counter this in society, in the workplace, in education, in sports, but also how we can help victims of sexual harassment and violence, in the justice chain but also in life. That letter arose from the heated up — I can't say "emerging" — #MeToo discussion earlier that month.
I am not going to repeat what I wrote in that letter, but tonight I would like to briefly clear up the misunderstanding that there are unclear standards for sexual harassment. I think we agree in society about rape and sexual assault, in short, sexual violence, especially about rape. This is clearly formulated in criminal law in Article 242. Sexual assault is in Article 246. For the sake of clarity, I would like to say once again: sexual assault is any coerced, indecent act.
In recent months, here and there in the debate, at least sometimes in the media, people have suggested that there is no clear standard for sexual harassment. That is not correct, because that standard exists. The General Equal Treatment Act contains the following definition of sexual harassment in approximately these terms: sexual harassment is any form of unwanted verbal, non-verbal or physical sexually oriented behavior with the purpose or effect of violating the dignity of another person. And that, you could say, in particular by creating an intimidating, hostile, degrading or humiliating environment. The central point here is violating the dignity of another through certain sexually explicit behavior. That's sexual harassment. I think that provides sufficient guidance to know how far you can go or - even better - which boundaries you really should not cross.
I would like to say, although I am interested in the idea expressed by Mrs Van Toorenburg, that there are also a number of standards in criminal law in that area. I mention indecency in Article 239 of Criminal Law — which is a minor sexual offense — or sexually intimidating behavior in the form of coercion, threat or insult. This is all also regulated in Criminal Law. I'm not going to bother you with naming the numbers.
Chair. I don't really see myself as a moral knight. I just think it is important that, especially when there is a very clear discussion going on within society - the #MeToo discussion - we once again identify together what the problem is. The MPs did that tonight. I am not going to go through all the reports again, which nevertheless indicate in detail that there is still a problem with sexual violence and sexual harassment in this society. I cited the 2014 Fundamental Rights Agency report in my letter, but I can also refer to reports from the Rutgers Foundation, which is certainly beyond doubt. The Sexual Health Monitor, for example, clearly indicates that there is still plenty of room for improvement.
In any case, what I wanted to make clear tonight - I think I did - is that we have clear rules, including in the area of ​​sexual harassment. This means that in society people can address each other about this and must continue to address it, even if the hashtag, #MeToo, has gradually faded away. I don't want to leave it at that.
Thanks for the handkerchief. It's not the emotion, it's the weather.
I would like to bring to your attention that tomorrow I have a working visit to Pretty Woman, an organization in Utrecht that will include a number of other organizations. Then it is about looking at tackling new online forms of sexual harassment, because they are now also available. Sexting, exposing and the like; they are simply new phenomena, new manifestations. We as a society have to work on this. We have to do something about that. As Minister of Justice, you can certainly be one of the first to address me about this. In short, we still have plenty of work to do together to reduce sexual violence and sexual harassment in society.
A few questions have come to my attention and I would like to answer them briefly. Mr Sjoerdsma asked when there will be an action plan to increase willingness to report. An initial conversation will take place shortly with the national leader of the Sexual Violence Centers. Based on the WODC report on the experience of victims of sexual violence, which was sent to you by my predecessor in office in September, that conversation will explore how victims of sexual violence can be motivated to report to the government for justice and care. One finding from the report offers special starting points. This is the finding that the environment of victims has a major influence on the decision whether or not to report to the police. Unfortunately, a large number of situations involving sexual violence and sexual harassment take place within a small circle of acquaintances and family. Discussions will also take place with other partners in the follow-up process. This will happen under the direction of my colleague for Legal Protection, Sander Dekker.

Ik denk dat het belangrijkste deel van mijn verhaal juist ging over de transitie. Een transitie doe je om een recept niet intact te laten maar om het op een andere manier te gaan doen. Mijn waarschuwing is dat wij moeten zorgen dat dat zo beheerst mogelijk gaat en dat we dat betaalbaar kunnen houden, omdat anders grote delen van deze samenleving afhaken. En dat is waar ik bang voor ben. Bovendien, zoals ik aan het begin zei, zitten hier twee bewindslieden die allebei vinden dat belastinggeld goed besteed moet worden en niet verspild moet worden. Dus de kosten zijn gewoon belangrijk. Ik denk dat de heer Van Raan dat wel met mij eens is, want hij weet ook wel dat misschien zijn achterban niet afhaakt maar te veel achterbannen wel als we dat niet op een goede manier doen. Hier ligt een taak.
Voorzitter, ik kan aan een volgend blokje beginnen: klimaat en energie. Ik begin met het klimaatakkoord. Waarom eigenlijk een klimaatakkoord? Waarom doen we niet gewoon wat we vinden dat gedaan moet worden? Dat is natuurlijk omdat een transitie niet een ding van de overheid is. De overheid produceert niet, ook geen elektriciteit. De overheid innoveert niet. De overheid is ook maar een beperkte gebruiker. Er zijn overheidsrollen, zeker: regie, wetgeving, financiële instrumenten. Maar waar het de overheid is, is het niet alleen het Rijk. Waar het het Rijk is, is het niet alleen EZK. Ik heb verschillende collega's die hieraan mee moeten doen. Dat vraagt dus om een akkoord, want ik ben het niet alleen en u bent het ook niet alleen.
Dat regeerakkoord is wat mij betreft de basis, maar het is ook een heel Hollands product. Ik heb eerder gezegd: zo Hollands als een vlaflip. Want het is een positieve uitruil. Het heeft even geduurd, maar het is een positieve uitruil. De ambitie is torenhoog. Daar heeft iedereen zijn eigen verhaal bij. De een noemt het zijn uitleg van het liberalisme, de ander noemt het rentmeesterschap of de Schepper. We hebben allemaal een andere manier om op hetzelfde doel uit te komen. Daar hebben we kosteneffectiviteit bovenop gezet, om op een niet-ideologische manier dat doel te halen. Daar hebben we dan ook nog een zeker vleugje polder overheen gegooid. In Frankrijk met Macron zouden we het op een andere manier doen, maar wij doen het met zo'n klimaatakkoord.
Ik heb het over een klimaatakkoord, want het vorige akkoord ging over energie en heette energieakkoord. Dit gaat over klimaat, dus noem ik het klimaatakkoord. Maar die akkoorden zijn wel degelijk verschillend. In het energieakkoord kwam het doel eigenlijk van de SER, niet van de regering of uit een regeerakkoord. Dat is hier wel het geval. Aangezien het daar niet uit de regering kwam, zijn er achteraf bezien ook weinig prijzen uitgedeeld voor de democratische legitimering van het energieakkoord in zijn eerdere vorm. Hier komt het echt uit het regeerakkoord. Er is één doel: het klimaatdoel uit het klimaatakkoord; die 49%. Dat betekent dat we hard moeten sturen op publiek belang. Het gaat niet om de deelbelangen van de deelnemers. Daar ging het bij het energieakkoord in essentie in zo'n SER-setting wel een beetje om. Ik heb er zelf aan meegedaan en terugkijkend zeg ik weleens tegen mezelf: Eric Wiebes, dat had je in jouw rol ook best anders kunnen doen. Maar dat heb ik niet gedaan. Daardoor is het op sommige punten toch een beetje een feest geweest van belangenbehartigingsorganisaties.
Ik denk dat hier — u zou dat van mij moeten verwachten, maar ik wil u niks in de mond leggen — het publiek belang bewaakt moet worden. Dat betekent dat de overheid niet alleen de regie moet nemen, maar ook doelen moet stellen en kaders moet meegeven. Het is niet de bedoeling dat er een overeenkomst komt tussen partijen aan tafel om het twee maal zo duur te doen als nodig. Ik ben hier nogal ferm op het publiek belang. Bij een klimaatakkoord — daarover moet je het kunnen hebben — moeten ook vrijheidsgraden bestaan. Maar het doel staat. Laat ik zo zeggen, ik ga niet overhandelen over het percentage. What also does not help is the fact that the ministry, Schiphol, the aviation sector and the EIA Commission. sit on each other's laps. Drafters and assessors of the EIA are married. Civil servants help draw up the Schiphol EIA, which they must then assess themselves. Schiphol will postpone the EIA for two years until a desired outcome is achieved. Several ministers and directors of Schiphol come from Shell; not an insignificant party within fossil and polluting aviation. Last week it also emerged that KLM contributes to the answers that MPs provide to this minister and her officials. So the question again: does the minister think she has managed to restore confidence? Please leave a comment.
Yet the minister manages to continue to amaze us. After each new low, I, along with many others, think that things can't get any worse. And yet it happens. Because last Friday's letter, in which the minister opens the doors wide to autonomous growth and cargo flights at Lelystad Airport, even the coalition did not see it coming, I gather from the reactions I have seen. This is nothing more than changing the rules of the game even though the competition started ten years ago. Abandoning the principle that Lelystad, if there is any expansion at all, must function as an overflow airport from Schiphol, is a hard slap in the face to people who perhaps still had a tiny bit of confidence in this minister and politicians, all those people in Overijssel, Gelderland, Friesland, the Veluwe and, for example, everyone who signed the petition we received last week, in the name of everything that has no voice: children, animals and nature. Because they should come first, and not push through a hopeless asphalt strip in the polder.
Chair. Now that the European Commission has also made it clear that forcing companies to move from Schiphol to Lelystad is not allowed, the minister must provide clarity today. She will soon have to confirm that Lelystad would only have a right to exist as a spillover from Schiphol, that the plug will be pulled if that is not possible and that freight and night flights will not be allowed at Lelystad Airport in any case. I have already indicated this in previous debates. As far as the SP is concerned, this debate is an excellent opportunity for the minister to show that she has a straight back, listens to the people she has spoken to and stands behind her previous words. The minister must show his true colors today.
